newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Cocoa seen locked in 70-stg range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Cocoa seen locked in 70-stg range.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Cocoa futures are likely to remain locked in a tight 1,000-1,070 stg range on September after having spiked up from last week's floor at 965, technical analysts said.
They called the market to open unchanged to three stg down.
"The market is not looking too bad in the short term," said Adrian Haylor, an analyst at Sucden.
"It has moved back into the range between 1,000 and 1,070 and I think I will stay in that range," he said. "I don't think it will go storming higher."
The initial resistance is pegged at the 40-day moving average of 1,062, followed by 1,070.
On the downside, a break below the 1,000 support would set the market back to 965, the low on July 24.
On Wedneday, New York's cocoa futures ended at at 1-1/2 week high on keen speculative buying amid lingering concerns about El Nino and the size of the upcoming Ivorian crop.
Continued concerns that a strong El Nino pattern could adversely impact cocoa crops -- particularly in Indonesia, Malaysia and Ecuador -- helped set a bullish tone.
Worries that recent dry weather in West Africa could affect the developing 1997/98 Ivorian main crop also underpinned sentiment.

Traders said there were rumours private forecaster Hans Kilian put the 1997/98 Ivorian main crop at 880,000 to 900,000 tonnes, which was higher than his previous forecast, they said, but below some expectations of around one million tonnes.
Reached in New Orleans, Kilian refused to comment.
The International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) said on Wednesday it was inviting bids for up to 4,250 tonnes of buffer stock cocoa by 1140 GMT Thursday.
Thursday is the last trading and tender day for spot July contract. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
